info.title: Djehuty
info.description:
Public data needs no token. For example, listing datasets:

```
curl https://example.com/v2/articles
```

## Authentication

Protected endpoints in both **v2** and **v3** need an API token in the
`Authorization` header. Both of these forms are accepted:

```
Authorization: token YOUR_TOKEN
Authorization: YOUR_TOKEN
```

### Getting a token

Tokens come from your account on the repository (deployed djehuty), not from this page: sign in,
open your dashboard, and under **Sessions and API tokens** create one. The
session token issued when you sign in works too, and stays valid until you sign
out.

### Using it

Send the token in the `Authorization` header on every request:

```
curl -H "Authorization: token YOUR_TOKEN" https://example.com/v2/account
curl -H "Authorization: token YOUR_TOKEN" https://example.com/v3/profile
```

When this reference is opened on a running instance, the **Authorize** button
(the lock) also lets you paste a token and try requests from the page directly.

post.summary: Upload a file to a dataset
post.description:
Stream-upload a single file into a draft dataset.

Request body must be ``multipart/form-data`` with one file part.

Query parameters:
- ``strict_check=1`` — reject empty files, duplicate MD5s, and MD5 mismatches; the ``md5`` parameter becomes required.
- ``md5`` — 32-character hex MD5 of the file's contents (required when ``strict_check=1``).

Responses:
- ``200`` — file accepted, ``{"location": "<base>/v3/file/<uuid>"}``
- ``400`` — empty file, malformed body, or MD5 mismatch
- ``403`` — account has no quota or no permission to edit dataset
- ``409`` — duplicate file (only when ``strict_check=1``)
- ``413`` — file exceeds remaining quota
- ``415`` — not multipart/form-data
